_comment: Template for an operator entry under data/operators/. One file per operator, filename = slug + '.json'. Copy this file, fill it in, and delete this comment field along with the guidance notes below.
name: Example Air Force
_type_note: "military" for air forces / navies / armies / government agencies, "commercial" for airlines and other private/civil operators. Drives which half of the /operators/ index this appears under.
_country_note: code must be a key that exists in src/svg-icons.js's `flags` object (falls back to a dashed placeholder flag otherwise).
_logo_note: Filename in src/assets/img/operators/ (see OPERATOR-LOGOS.md), or null to fall back to a monogram badge.
_website_note: Optional - the operator's official homepage. Only fill in a URL you've actually verified; leave null rather than guess.
tagline: One sentence capturing what makes this operator distinctive.
bio: First bio paragraph - founding, mission, place in aviation history.
Second bio paragraph (optional) - what's special about them today.
_matchPattern_note: A case-insensitive regex (as a plain string, no slashes) tested against every aircraft's operators[].name field across data/aircraft/*.json. Any aircraft whose operator name matches gets pulled onto this operator's page, using that SPECIFIC operator entry's own status/since/fleetSize/homeBase for the In Service/Retired split - so write it broad enough to catch real variant phrasings ("Royal Air Force (as Dakota)", "RAF Bomber Command") but not so broad it accidentally matches an unrelated operator. Word-boundary (\b) short codes like RAF/USAF avoid matching inside longer unrelated words.
